title: Three Months and One Short Page
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：perspective　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 perspective 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the writer ① offered the perspective that no reader in the study would have described, and he said the offering was the whole of the month. The ② perspective, meaning the view itself and not the page, ran three months and stayed undescribed in the book; a perspective, he said, is the only thing in a study that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ perspective in that study had the same short page beside it, and the ④ perspective at the far shelf, meaning the draft they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A perspective, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the writer said the describing is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the perspective was the whole of the matter, meaning the wisdom and not the view. The ⑥ perspective, meaning the wisdom and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; perspective, he said, is either something you offer or the only word that means both a view and a wisdom. He said the wisdom is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ perspective had become a line in a manuscript, and the manuscript had become an argument about the short page. The ⑧ perspective of the whole thing, the writer wrote in January, was one study and three months of describing; perspective, he said, is either the draft at the far shelf or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ perspective I remember is the view described in the manuscript, which closed in 1963 and is still described as the quietest in the study. A ⑩ perspective, my mother said in 1965, is the only view that improves by being described; every perspective, she said, is a wisdom that has agreed to look like a view. She said the wisdom was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 视角；观点（指书斋里每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 视角；观点（指那种视角本身，与薄薄的书页相对）
C. 固定搭配：offer the perspective 提供这一种视角
D. n. 视角；观点（指留给孩子们誊的那一份）
E. n. 视角之事（抽象总称，指一处书斋的视角之事）
F. n. 视角；观点（指手稿里写到、被描述的那一种）
G. n. 视角、见识（指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 见识（抽象总称，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: offered the perspective that no reader in the study would have described
The perspective, meaning the view itself and not the page
the perspective at the far shelf
the perspective was the whole of the matter
the perspective had become a line in a manuscript
The perspective of the whole thing
A perspective, my mother said in 1965

answers.why: offer the perspective 意为“提供这一种视角”，1956 年那位写作者把书斋里没有一位读者肯描述的一种视角做了一遍。
perspective 意为“视角；观点”，指那种视角本身而不是薄薄的书页，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被描述。
perspective 意为“视角；观点”，指书斋里每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一页薄薄的书页。
perspective 意为“视角；观点”，指最远那层书架的留给孩子们誊的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
perspective 意为“视角、见识”，指一件事里人人都读却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这种见识就是那件事的全部。
perspective 意为“见识”，指人人都读却无人提起的那样东西而不是那种视角，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
perspective 意为“视角；观点”，指手稿里写到、被描述的那一种，到 1961 年这一种成了手稿里的一行。
perspective 意为“视角之事”，写作者一月写道，整件事的视角之事是一处书斋和三个月份的描述。
perspective 意为“视角；观点”，我记得的是手稿里描述过的那一种，1963 年写就了，至今仍被说成书斋里最安静的一种。
perspective 为抽象总称，母亲 1965 年说，视角是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的视角。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1956 年那位写作者提供了书斋里没有一位读者肯描述的一种视角，他说这一遍才是那个月份的全部。（offer the perspective）
那种视角，指的是那种视角本身而不是薄薄的书页，经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被描述。（perspective）
那处书斋里每一种视角旁边都有同一页薄薄的书页。（perspective）
最远那层书架那种视角，指的是他们留给孩子们誊的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（perspective）
叔叔说这种见识就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那种视角。（perspective）
